_note: What Grandma Tome says when the farmer talks to them (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; the gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction (gift_birthday on their birthday) (gifts in data/villagers/tome.json). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Eighty-one autumns today, and still the persimmons ripen on time. Thank you, child.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A present, on my birthday? You'll make an old woman cry in the street.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Still here? Don't mind me, I'm only resting my knees.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Go on, the field won't hoe itself. I'll be here.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I put you in my last letter again. My son wrote back that he'd like to meet you, come New Year.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The persimmon by the shrine has more buds than last year. I counted them, twice.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Come in for tea whenever the lamp's lit. You needn't knock. Family doesn't knock.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: When you walk by, the morning feels a little longer. In a good way.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My husband used to keep that field, you know. He'd be glad to see it green.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I made too much pickled radish again. Come by the house when you're hungry.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You've the same habit he had. Looking at the sky before you look at the soil.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Cold enough to crack the water jar. Wrap your neck, child.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Winter is for mending baskets and waiting. The ground needs its sleep too.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh, good morning. You're the one who took the old farm up the hill?

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: I come to the shrine every morning. At my age, you say thank you early.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Hm? Ah, the new farmer. The path gets muddy by the pond. Mind your step.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Young people don't stay long in this village. Let's see about you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: On Sundays I walk round the shrine twice. Once for me, once for him.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The plum by my house has opened. Spring always comes in quietly here.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Sow the turnips before the rains. That's what my mother told me.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: This heat... Drink water before you're thirsty. And wear a hat.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Listen to the cicadas. In my day we counted them to fall asleep.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The persimmons are turning. Soon the whole hill smells sweet.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Harvest time. Everyone is busy, and the evenings come in early.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: The pond is calm today. Days like this are a gift.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My knees say rain tomorrow. They're right more often than the radio.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: For me? Oh my... this is just what I like.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Thank you, child. I'll make tea and think of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: How kind. I'll put it to good use, thank you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh, thank you. You needn't bring an old woman anything.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Hm. Thank you... but my teeth and I don't get on with this.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Oh dear. I'd rather not have that, if it's all the same to you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You already gave me something today. Keep that for yourself.
